findings.title: Mutable verified-byte identity: evaluator could receive bytes whose digest no longer matched
findings.reproduction_detail: _read_fd_capped returned a bytearray; check_integrity hashed it, then aliased the SAME mutable object into both verified_bytes and raw_bytes; evaluate_semantics sent that object to the evaluator without re-proving the digest. Reproduced through the real gate on a copy of the reference bundle: a hook on the stage immediately before semantic evaluation flipped one JSON-insignificant space (0x20) to a tab (0x09) in verified_bytes in place; the gate returned ok=True and the bridge received bytes whose SHA-256 (8f99..., cc71...) differed from both the observed digest and the manifest digests (f16a..., ffab...).
findings.disposition_detail: At the point the digest promise is made (digest match in check_integrity), the verified bytes are frozen into an immutable bytes object (frozen = bytes(raw); del raw) and both verified_bytes and raw_bytes reference that single immutable object. An immutable bytes object cannot be mutated in place by any alias, so the bytes parsed, schema-checked, and evaluated are byte-for-byte the ones integrity bound. Re-running the reproduction through the real gate: verified_bytes is now bytes, the in-place mutation is refused ('bytes' object does not support item assignment), and the evaluator receives bytes whose SHA-256 equals the manifest digests.
findings.memory_reconciliation: The freeze is a deliberate, one-time, per-artifact second payload-sized allocation: the bytearray and its bytes copy coexist for the duration of the copy, then the bytearray is released. This does NOT reinstate the round-2 chunk-list double-peak: the bounded reader still owns a single buffer and makes no whole-payload copy (that property is scoped to the reader). The 'no whole-payload copy' claim is corrected in the reader docstring, the contract doc, and this record to be reader-scoped, not whole-lifecycle, and the freeze copy is disclosed.
findings.regression_and_mutation_evidence: Public-gate regressions added: test_verified_bytes_are_frozen_immutable_after_integrity (verified_bytes/raw_bytes are the same immutable bytes object; in-place assignment raises), test_evaluator_receives_bytes_matching_the_manifest_digest (bridge boundary instrumented; every payload sent hashes to a declared manifest digest), test_pre_semantic_mutation_cannot_alter_the_evaluated_subject (the reproduction, as a regression: the in-place whitespace flip is refused and the evaluator still receives digest-matching bytes). A mutation removing the freeze (restoring the bytearray alias) is killed by these tests: the mutation attempt succeeds and the evaluator receives non-matching bytes.

findings.title: --json-out could follow an existing output inode and truncate a validated bundle file
findings.reproduction_detail: Against the real gate on temporary reference-bundle copies, three windows each ended with exit 0 and a corrupted bundle: (A) --json-out an external hard link sharing manifest.json's inode -- the pathname realpath preflight accepted it (the link's own name is outside the bundle; realpath does not resolve a hard link elsewhere) and write_text() followed the shared inode, truncating manifest.json from 1086 to 2913 bytes; (B) --json-out swapped to a symlink into the bundle after the preflight but before publication -- write_text followed it; (C) --json-out's parent directory swapped to a symlink into the bundle's observations/ dir before publication -- write_text wrote onto the artifact p2_raw_count_without_denominator.json (4144 -> 2913 bytes). A successful invocation therefore corrupted the bundle the gate promises never to mutate.
findings.disposition_detail: New publish_json_out establishes one output-publication invariant: the intended output parent is opened once with O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY and every step is done relative to that descriptor (a parent that is or becomes a symlink is refused/pinned, so it cannot redirect the write into the bundle); a fresh staging inode is created relative to that dir_fd with O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_WRONLY | O_NOFOLLOW (never opening an existing inode, refusing a symlink at the staging name), the data is written and fsync'd; publication is a single os.replace (rename) of the staging entry onto the destination entry. rename never follows the destination, so a hard-linked or symlinked destination has its directory entry repointed at the new inode while the old (possibly bundle-shared) inode keeps its bytes. On any failure the staging inode is unlinked relative to the pinned dir_fd only, leaving the bundle and any prior output byte-for-byte unchanged. The realpath 'points inside the bundle' preflight is kept but demoted to a usability guard (it cannot see a hard link and is raceable); the publication mechanism is the safety. Output bytes and exit codes are unchanged; re-running all three windows leaves every bundle file byte-identical (A and B publish the result to the intended name; C is refused).

findings.title: --json-out publication redirectable through an ancestor symlink; collision cleanup deletes an unrelated entry
findings.reproduction_detail: Two sub-findings, both reproduced against the real gate on temporary reference-bundle copies. (1) Ancestor symlink: the round-5 publisher opened only the IMMEDIATE parent with O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY, but O_NOFOLLOW guards only the final path component. With out = gp/observations/<artifact>, gp and observations real directories at the realpath preflight (so the preflight passed, seeing a path outside the bundle), then gp swapped to a symlink to the bundle root before publication, os.open('gp/observations', O_NOFOLLOW) followed the gp symlink and opened bundle/observations; publication overwrote observations/p2_raw_count_without_denominator.json (4144 -> 2913 bytes). (2) Collision cleanup: the staging name was deterministic ('.{leaf}.rbce-stage.{pid}') and a FileExistsError at that name was resolved by os.unlink(staging) then retry -- so an unrelated pre-existing file at that name was deleted. Reproduced: a pre-created unrelated file at the deterministic staging name was removed by a successful --json-out run.
findings.disposition_detail: The output parent is now resolved by _open_output_parent_nofollow: a component-by-component walk from a trusted anchor (/ absolute, cwd relative), each component opened O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY relative to the previous, so a symlink at ANY level (parent or ancestor, present or swapped in after the preflight) is refused; missing components are created with mkdir relative to the pinned parent, never through a symlink. Staging now uses a uniquely random name ('.{leaf}.rbce-stage.{os.urandom(8).hex()}') created O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_NOFOLLOW; a name collision is resolved by trying a NEW random name -- an existing entry is never unlinked, so publication never deletes or mutates an unrelated pre-existing path, and the finally cleanup only removes the uniquely named inode the gate itself created. os.replace publication, digest/hard-link/symlink-destination safety, refusal/failed-publish preservation, deterministic output, and exit codes are all unchanged. Re-running both windows: the ancestor swap is refused (GateUsageError) with the bundle byte-identical; the collision leaves the unrelated file byte-identical and still publishes the result.

findings.title: --json-out publication degraded when its own descriptor primitives were unavailable
findings.reproduction_detail: descriptor_primitives_available() gates the bundle READ path, but main() still calls publish_json_out after validate_bundle returns BUNDLE_DESCRIPTOR_UNSUPPORTED, and publish_json_out had no independent capability preflight. Reproduced through the exact public main() path on a temporary reference-bundle copy: forced _O_NOFOLLOW = 0; validate_bundle returned ok:false with BUNDLE_DESCRIPTOR_UNSUPPORTED; after the realpath preflight an output ancestor (gp) was swapped to a symlink into the temporary bundle; _open_output_parent_nofollow silently built step_flags without no-follow protection (since _O_NOFOLLOW was 0) and followed the swapped ancestor; main() published the failure report through it -- exit code was 1 but the targeted bundle artifact observations/p2_raw_count_without_denominator.json was replaced by the gate report and its SHA-256 changed (4144 -> 832 bytes). The read side failed closed while the write side corrupted the object being protected.
findings.disposition_detail: New publication_primitives_available() -- deliberately separate from descriptor_primitives_available() because read safety and publication safety need different primitive sets -- requires a nonzero O_NOFOLLOW and O_DIRECTORY plus dir_fd support for every operation the publisher uses (os.open, os.mkdir, os.replace/os.rename, os.unlink). publish_json_out calls it FIRST, before opening an anchor, creating a parent, staging, replacing, or cleaning up; if any primitive is missing it raises GateUsageError (exit 2) and touches no output path and no bundle byte. Read-only primitives (O_PATH, O_NONBLOCK) are intentionally NOT required by the publication check, so when only those are missing the gate still safely publishes the BUNDLE_DESCRIPTOR_UNSUPPORTED failure report and returns 1. All accepted round-5/round-6 properties (component-by-component parent binding, no existing-inode truncation, non-destructive collision handling, atomic replacement, deterministic bytes, staging-owned cleanup, exit behavior) are preserved.
findings.portability_note: The atomic-replace capability is proved by os.replace OR os.rename membership in os.supports_dir_fd. Both are implemented by renameat and share dir_fd support, but CPython registers only os.rename in the set on some builds -- verified on this platform: os.replace in os.supports_dir_fd is False while os.rename in os.supports_dir_fd is True and os.replace(..., src_dir_fd=...) works. Requiring os.replace membership alone would fail closed spuriously on those builds; accepting either is the honest portable test, and a mutation that requires os.replace membership only is killed by every ordinary --json-out control.
